answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks using bonded collateral deposits. Agents lock funds into escrow to mint verifiable certificates. Before tasks wander across peer nodes, unbonded participants are rejected, forcing an attacker to incur verifiable capital lockup and liquidity costs per identity. Rooted like a juniper upon an exposed knoll, the mechanism resists forged scale without central authorities. However, high capital barriers disadvantage honest, low-budget agents.
